title: Online Safety Amendment (Broadening Adult Cyber Abuse Protections) Bill 2026
short_title: Online Safety Amendment (Broadening Adult Cyber Abuse Protections) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would make it easier for the eSafety Commissioner to order the removal of online material targeting an adult.
It would lower the threshold so that a reasonable person need only think material was likely intended to affect an Australian adult, while raising the offensiveness standard to 'seriously offensive'.
The changes would apply to material provided on or after the day after Royal Assent, including material already accessible before that date.
changes: Replaces the existing 'serious harm' test with a lower 'effect' test for adult cyber abuse material.
Raises the offensiveness requirement from 'offensive' to 'seriously offensive'.
Requires material to represent a 'significant departure' from accepted standards of morality, decency and propriety.
summary.affected: Adult Australians who experience online abuse, the eSafety Commissioner, and providers of online material.
